method: SORTED BY EYE by the composited-frame lane, from contact sheets of the SAME RUN, before any row of census-c*.json was opened beyond the four progress columns the capture prints per site. The canvas arm and the composited arm are the SAME BATTLE at the SAME INSTANT (battle_decide --composite=1 splits its driver at the photograph: canvas jpg, then one Page.captureScreenshot ~200 ms later, then the measurement), so canvas-vs-composited is a paired comparison with rater held fixed. That pairing is the point: comparing my composited sort against the PREVIOUS lane's canvas sort would confound the treatment with the rater, and the two raters differ by ~10 points of bad on identical pictures (reported separately). Sites PLACE did not move AND whose two arms photograph the same picture (measured, frame diff <= 3/255) carry one verdict into both arms rather than being judged twice; 21 moved sites and 9 TONE-re-pick sites were judged in both arms.

rubric.good: all bodies read immediately as separate figures; what is behind them differs from them in value or is open; the ground plane reads; no single surface owns the frame
rubric.acceptable: readable but compromised — one side of the cast is low-contrast, or one surface owns half the frame, or the place is odd but legible
rubric.bad: a body is effectively lost (inside foliage, or at its background's own value, or in near-black), or one surface owns the frame with nothing else in it, or the party is in a hole / on a roof / behind clutter

departure: The previous lane's departure is honoured verbatim: party-on-party overlap is a property of the 27 mm two-shot present everywhere and is NOT scored. TWO CLAUSES ADDED FOR THE COMPOSITED ARM, and both are about what the player sees rather than about the place: (1) a body substantially covered by a DOM panel is 'effectively lost' exactly as one covered by geometry — but a NAMEPLATE clipped by a panel is recorded and NOT scored, because it is a UI-layout defect uniform across sites; (2) the composited frame carries battle_turnbased's .ebb-vig radial vignette and .ebb-scrim foot wash, which are part of the shipped presentation, so a body the grade pushes to its background's value fails the same clause a body the world puts there fails. INSTRUMENT ARTEFACTS NOT SCORED: the ?rt=1 debug text line and the 'music off' toast are the harness's, not the game's.
